reason: The text contains multiple regular human characters with extensive dialogue, emotions, and stated opinions. Jonathan (the armor-bearer's companion) displays faith and conviction in his speeches about God's ability to deliver (יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לָ֑נוּ). The armor-bearer responds with encouragement and loyalty (עֲשֵׂ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר בִּלְבָבֶךָ). Saul shows emotional reactions and makes pronouncements about sin and punishment. The people respond emotionally to events, express fear and eagerness, and ultimately defend Jonathan with passionate conviction (הֲיוֹנָתָן יָמוּת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה הַיְשׁוּעָה הַגְּדוֹלָה). Even unnamed soldiers and individuals within the crowd ('אִישׁ מֵֽהָעָם) have lines expressing opinions. All these characters exhibit both emotion and stated perspectives on events.
